transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope it's okay if I just start with work stuff? 

Well, I'm here because... they recently made me the acting workflow lead at the warehouse where I work. Which is a good thing, really, I'm very grateful for the opportunity. But, um, ever since it happened, I've just been... well, I guess I've been walking into the building already tense. 

I hate to even admit this, because I always try to be an easygoing guy and a good team player, but I've been snapping a little bit over minor SAP errors. And, um, I’ve missed a few cycle-count deadlines, which I never, ever used to do. It's embarrassing, honestly. And then I get home and I'm just so drained I can't even bring myself to play basketball or work on my sketches anymore. 

I just want to get back to doing a good job and being myself, you know? I hope that makes sense... is that the kind of thing I should be bringing up?

You mentioned that you don't feel like playing basketball or working on your sketches anymore. Have you lost interest in these activities altogether, or do you still want to do them but just feel too drained?

Oh, um, that's a really good question. I... I definitely still want to do them. I haven't, like, given up on them or anything bad like that. I really love sketching, and the guys I play hoops with are great. 

It's just... yeah, I think it's mostly just feeling a little too worn out after my shifts right now. I get home and I just sort of sit on the couch and... the night just gets away from me. I really hope it doesn't sound like I'm just being lazy or completely dropping my hobbies. I really am trying my best to stay active, it's just been a little harder lately with the new role. 

Does that... does that answer your question okay? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right for you.
Have you found yourself feeling worse about your performance at work or been harder on yourself since becoming the acting workflow lead?

Well, um... I mean, I guess I've been a little disappointed in myself with the missed deadlines. I really pride myself on being reliable, so it stings a bit when I drop the ball. But I wouldn't say I'm being, like, overly hard on myself or feeling terrible about my overall performance. 

I know there's a learning curve with any new position, and I'm really trying to focus on the positive and just, you know, do better the next day. I don't want you to think I'm sitting around beating myself up all the time. I'm just... trying to figure out how to manage the new responsibilities, I guess. 

Is it normal to feel a little bit of that pressure when you step up at work? I hope I'm not making too big a deal out of it.
Since becoming the acting workflow lead, have you found yourself feeling anxious or worried most days, even when there’s no immediate problem at work?

Um, no, I wouldn't say I'm anxious most days. I mean, I definitely feel that tension I mentioned when I first walk in, just wanting to make sure I'm on top of things. But I'm not sitting around worrying all the time when there's nothing going on. 

I really try to leave work at work, you know? I don't want to be one of those guys who brings all their stress home and lets it ruin their whole day. So, no, I don't think I'm constantly worried. I just... I just want to do a good job when I'm there. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm not giving the impression that I'm totally falling apart or anything.
Have you noticed yourself feeling down or sad most days, even if it's not overwhelming or constant?

Um, no... no, I really wouldn't say I've been feeling sad or down most days. I mean, sure, I get a little frustrated when I'm tired or when things pile up at the warehouse, but I'm definitely not walking around feeling depressed or anything like that. 

I really try to keep a good attitude. I know a lot of people have it way worse, so I don't want to sound like I'm complaining or throwing a pity party just because I'm a little stressed out with the new role. I'm usually a pretty upbeat guy, I promise. 

I hope it's okay that I don't feel that way? I just want to be honest with you, and I really don't think I'm dealing with, like, real sadness or anything.
Have you been feeling a noticeable lack of energy or fatigue almost every day, even when you haven't been particularly busy or stressed at work?

Well, um... no, I wouldn't say I'm feeling fatigued almost every day. I mean, sure, I'm a little tired at the end of a long shift, but that's just part of the job, right? It's a physical job, being on your feet in the warehouse all day, so I think it's pretty normal to be a little wiped out by the time I get home. 

But I'm definitely not, like, dragging myself out of bed or feeling exhausted when I haven't even done anything. I try to make sure I get enough sleep so I can be ready for the next day. I don't want to sound like I'm slacking off or can't handle the physical part of the work. 

I'm holding up okay in that department, I think. Is it alright that I'm just feeling regular tired and not, like, completely drained?
Have you noticed that the activities you usually enjoy, like sketching or playing basketball, are less satisfying or pleasurable to you lately, even when you do manage to do them?

Um, well... I guess I haven't really noticed a difference, to be honest. I mean, I haven't had a ton of time for sketching lately, just with trying to make sure I'm doing everything right at the warehouse. But when I do get a minute to myself, or if I shoot some hoops, it's still good. 

I definitely don't want you to think I'm just sitting around doing nothing or losing interest in my life. I still like the things I like, you know? I'm just prioritizing work right now because I want to prove I can handle this workflow lead position. 

So, yeah, I'd say I still enjoy my hobbies just fine. Is that what you're looking for? I just want to make sure I'm answering these right.
Have you noticed any trouble focusing or keeping your attention on tasks at work or home lately?

Um, no, my focus is pretty good, actually. I mean, sure, sometimes there's a lot going on at the warehouse, and it can be a little distracting with the forklifts and people yelling across the floor, but I definitely wouldn't say I'm having trouble paying attention. 

I really try to stay locked in on what I'm doing. I know they're counting on me as the workflow lead, so I make sure I double-check my clipboards and the inventory screens. I don't want anyone thinking I'm scatterbrained or dropping the ball, you know? I'm usually really organized.

So, yeah, my concentration is totally fine. I hope that's okay? I just want to reassure you that I'm keeping on top of things at work.
Have you had any trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or waking up too early in the morning lately?

Um, well, my sleep has been... it's been pretty okay, I think. I mean, I try to get to bed at a decent hour so I'm fresh for the morning shift. Sometimes it takes a little bit to wind down after being on my feet all day, but I wouldn't call it trouble falling asleep. Just, you know, normal unwinding.

I definitely don't want you to think I'm lying awake all night stressing out or anything like that. I know how important rest is to do a good job, and I really want to be sharp for the warehouse. Once I'm out, I'm usually out until my alarm goes off. 

So I think my sleep is totally normal. I hope that's the kind of answer you need? I'm just trying to make sure I'm giving you the right picture.
Have you found yourself feeling guilty or like you're not good enough because of any mistakes or missed deadlines at work lately?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I try really hard not to make mistakes in the first place, you know? I always double-check everything before I sign off on a shipment. 

Sure, sometimes things get backed up, but that's just the nature of the warehouse, it's not because I'm not good enough or anything. I definitely don't sit around feeling guilty. I know I'm a hard worker and I'm doing my best to show them I deserve the lead spot. 

I wouldn't want you to think I'm down on myself or anything like that. I'm pretty confident in my work. Is that... does that make sense? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you felt so overwhelmed by your new responsibilities at work that it's been hard to function normally in other parts of your life, like with family, friends, or your usual routines?

Um, well... I wouldn't say I can't function or anything. I'm still getting up and going to work every day, you know? But, um... I guess things have been a little bit of a juggle lately. 

I mean, my supervisor did sort of mention some missed cycle-count deadlines during a check-in recently. But it wasn't a huge deal, just a reminder to stay on top of things, which I totally understand. I'm really trying to make sure that doesn't happen again. 

And, well, I guess I haven't been playing basketball with the guys as much... or doing my sketching. But that's just because I want to make sure I'm putting all my energy into being a good workflow lead, you know? It's not that I can't function, it's just... work has been taking up a lot of my focus, and I want to do a good job for them. 

I hope it doesn't sound like I'm falling apart or anything. I'm just trying to be really dedicated. Is it normal to put your hobbies on hold when you get a promotion like this? I just want to make sure I'm handling this the right way.
Have you found yourself feeling like you're not capable or doubting your abilities at work, even though you're trying your best?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I definitely don't feel incapable. I know I have the skills for the job, you know? I've been in the warehouse a long time. 

Sure, maybe there are moments where I have to double-check my own work, just to be absolutely certain I'm doing things right for the new role. But that's just being thorough, right? It's not because I'm doubting myself. I just really want to prove to management that they made the right choice by giving me the lead spot. 

I definitely don't want you to think I'm second-guessing myself all the time or that I can't handle it. I'm actually really committed to making it work. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right so you can see I'm doing okay with it all.
Have you found yourself feeling less confident about your abilities at work since becoming the acting workflow lead, even if you're still trying your best?

Um, no, I wouldn't say I'm less confident. I mean, I know I just said I double-check things, but that's really just me being careful, you know? It's a new position, so I just want to be sure everything is perfect. 

I definitely still believe I can do the job. I wouldn't want you to think I'm losing my edge or anything like that. I'm just... I'm just taking it seriously and trying to be the best lead I can be. I'm sure anyone would want to be a little extra careful when they step up, right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right impression, that I'm still feeling strong about my work.
Have you noticed yourself putting in less effort at work or in other areas of your life lately, even though you still care about doing a good job?

Oh, no... no, definitely not less effort. Um, if anything, I feel like I'm trying harder than ever, you know? Like I was saying earlier, I really want to do right by management for trusting me with this lead spot, so I'm putting in all the focus I possibly can. 

I mean, I guess it's true I'm not putting effort into my hobbies right now, like the basketball or my sketching, but that's just so I can give everything I have to the warehouse. I really hope I'm not coming across like someone who slacks off or doesn't care, because I've always prided myself on being a really hard worker. 

I'm doing everything I can to keep up and do a good job. Is it okay that I'm prioritizing work like that right now? I just want to make sure you know I'm really dedicated and not just, you know, giving up on things.
Have you found yourself feeling like you're not as good at your job as you used to be since becoming the acting workflow lead?

No, I wouldn't say I'm not as good at it. I mean, I'm still the same worker I was before, you know? I still have all the same knowledge about how the floor runs and where everything goes. 

I guess the actual tasks are a little different now that I'm organizing the workflow instead of just pulling orders, so there's a learning curve. But I don't feel like I'm worse at my job. I'm just... adjusting to the new responsibilities, which takes a little time for anybody, right? 

I really don't want to sound like I'm failing at this or that I'm not cut out for it. I'm still pulling my weight and making sure the shift runs smoothly. I hope that makes sense? I just want to be clear that I'm still a good employee, even if I'm still figuring out the lead stuff.
Have you noticed any days where you just don't feel motivated to do anything, even things you usually look forward to?

Um, no, I wouldn't say I have days where I'm completely unmotivated. I mean, sure, sometimes I'm a little tired when my alarm goes off, but I always get up and go to work. I never just stay in bed or anything like that. 

I know I mentioned earlier that I haven't been playing basketball or sketching as much, but that's really just because I'm focusing so much energy on the new lead position, not because I don't care about them anymore. I still look forward to doing those things again once I get into a better rhythm at the warehouse. 

I'm definitely still motivated to do a good job and to take care of my responsibilities. I wouldn't want you to think I'm just sitting around doing nothing, you know? I'm still keeping busy. Does that sound like a normal way to handle a big change at work? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things are going.
Have you found yourself feeling worse about your abilities or performance at work lately, even if only mildly, since becoming the acting workflow lead?

Um, no, I wouldn't say I feel worse about my abilities. I mean, I know I'm capable of doing the job, and I know I have the skills for it. I've been at the warehouse a long time, so I know how things operate. 

I guess... maybe I just feel a little pressure to make sure I'm doing it exactly right? Because I really want management to see that they made the right choice. But I definitely don't feel like I'm bad at it or anything like that. I'm just trying to be really careful and thorough. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound insecure about my work? I just want to make sure I'm meeting expectations. It's pretty normal to want to double-check yourself when you get a promotion, isn't it? I just want to be the best lead I can be.
Have you found yourself feeling like you're not as competent or valuable at work since becoming the acting workflow lead, even if only slightly?

No, not at all. I definitely don't feel less valuable. If anything, I think I'm more valuable now because I'm taking on these extra responsibilities and helping the whole shift run, right? 

I know I'm competent. Management wouldn't have asked me to step up if they didn't think I could handle it. I mean, sure, it's a lot to juggle, and maybe I'm a little stressed trying to make sure I don't let anyone down, but that's just because I care about doing a good job. 

I wouldn't want you to think I'm doubting myself or feeling useless. I'm still a really hard worker, and I'm contributing a lot to the team. That's a good thing, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right so you don't think I'm falling apart at work or anything.
Have you found that even the things you usually enjoy, like hanging out with friends or watching your favorite shows, just don’t feel as good or interesting to you lately?

Um, no, I wouldn't say that. I still enjoy my shows and, you know, hanging out with people. I mean, I might be a little more tired after a long shift, so maybe I don't go out quite as much as I used to, but when I do, I still have a good time. 

It's not like I'm sitting there feeling miserable or bored. I still laugh at the same comedies and enjoy catching up with my buddies. I'm just prioritizing getting enough rest so I can be sharp for work the next day. 

I wouldn't want you to think I'm just isolating myself or losing interest in my life outside the warehouse. I'm still me, you know? Just... a slightly busier version of me right now. That makes sense, doesn't it? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right impression.
Have you noticed a decrease in your interest or enjoyment in activities you used to look forward to, like sketching or playing basketball, even when you have the time to do them?

Um... well, I guess I haven't really been showing up for basketball lately. And, yeah, my usual sketching time has kind of disappeared. But I wouldn't say I've lost interest in them! It's just... work is sort of taking over my life right now. 

I'm trying so hard to get everything right, but... um... well, to be honest, I did have a performance check-in recently where my supervisor had to bring up some missed cycle-count deadlines. I was pretty embarrassed about it, to be honest with you. 

So I've just been putting all my focus into fixing that and making sure I don't drop the ball again, which just means putting the fun stuff on hold for a bit. I think that just shows I'm dedicated to fixing my mistakes, right? I just really don't want management—or you—to think I can't handle things. It's normal to have to sacrifice some hobbies when you're trying to get the hang of a new role, isn't it?
